Diego — thanks for the heads up, I've sketched out an initial acceptance plan below based on what we've used on prior POCs. Open to tightening numbers if product wants to be more conservative.

Acceptance thresholds (final test):
- Win-rate (A vs B) delta: absolute difference <= 1.5 percentage points in favor of chosen variant (sample-weighted)
- Hallucination rate (measured on labeled long-form subset): <= 0.8%
- Concise-answer helpfulness: mean score >= 4.2/5 on 600-sample eval (stratified by prompt type)
- P95 generation latency (p50 token length): <= 650ms

Sampling plan:
- Holdout evaluation set: 600 prompts (200 long-form labelled for hallucination; 400 short/concise)
- Random bootstrap across traffic slices (peak vs off-peak) to avoid time-of-day skew

Canary rollout proposal:
- Phase 1: 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor win-rate and hallucination signals hourly
- Auto-rollback triggers (anyone of): win-rate delta <= -3.0 pp vs baseline OR hallucination rate increase > 1.5x baseline OR error rate spike > 0.5%
- Phase 2: if Phase 1 stable, 25% for 24h then full rollout

Owners & instrumentation:
- Preflight runs & sampling: Marissa Cole (QA)
- Canary orchestration & fallback route: Monica Patel (Infra/Deploy)
- Monitoring dashboards / alert sweeps: Karthik (Product/Monitoring)

I'll prepare a short doc with the exact test harness calls and the Grafana/alert links. Diego, can you confirm Acme's preferred window for the 5% canary? Also we should add the PII/privacy test Marissa mentioned — suggest adding that to the preflight checklist and make it a hard stop for acceptance.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
